summary: Western passports — the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas — enter Guatemala visa-free for up to 90 days, a stay shared across the CA-4 zone with El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua. Other nationalities need a consular visa, and some also require a security-vetted "consulted" visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Indian nationals holding a valid visa of the United States, Canada or a Schengen state do not need a Guatemalan visa, according to the Foreign Ministry's visa page (archived November 2024; the live address now redirects to the ministry's home page). No length of stay is stated. No official source we could read extends this to other nationalities: IGM's entry requirements and country classification pages do not mention it, and the published visa regulation (AMN-04-2025) returns "not found". Confirm with a Guatemalan consulate before relying on it.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Guatemala — Visas para extranjeros

fee.notes: USD 50 for a single entry. A multiple-entry tourist visa, valid for 90 days, costs USD 150.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Guatemala.

source.name: UK Foreign Office — Guatemala entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only for travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission (parts of South America and Africa). Not needed on direct arrivals from North America or Europe.

source.name: WHO — Countries with risk of yellow fever transmission and countries requiring yellow fever vaccination

travelInsurance.text: No official source states a travel insurance requirement for entering Guatemala. IGM's list of entry requirements does not include insurance. Private hospitals expect payment or proof of insurance up front, so medical cover is worth having.

source.name: Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración — Requisitos de ingreso a Guatemala

onwardTicket.text: IGM lists a return air ticket, or other transport that guarantees your departure from the country, among the requirements for entering Guatemala, along with a hotel booking or the name of a contact in the country.

source.name: Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración — Requisitos de ingreso a Guatemala

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show means of support for their stay.

source.name: Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración — Requisitos de ingreso a Guatemala

declarations.name: Regional Traveller Sworn Declaration (Declaración Jurada Regional de Viajero)
declarations.submitWindow: Online before you enter or leave Guatemala; terminals are also available on arrival before immigration
declarations.text: Every traveller, or the head of a family travelling together, entering or leaving Guatemala must complete the online sworn declaration on the tax and customs authority (SAT) portal. You receive a confirmation by email: print it or keep a screenshot of its QR code. It can also be filled in at terminals on arrival just before immigration, but that can delay your entry.

source.name: Superintendencia de Administración Tributaria (SAT) — Declaración Jurada Regional de Viajero portal

currencyLimits.text: Cash of USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: SAT — Electronic Traveler's Declaration

notes: The Government of Canada notes that customs authorities may enforce strict regulations on the import or export of items such as antiquities and artefacts; the UK Foreign Office says you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

payments.text: No official source describes how widely cards are accepted in Guatemala. The UK Foreign Office notes that British pounds often cannot be exchanged and US dollars are much easier, warns of tampered ATMs and says it is safer to change money in hotels, banks or exchange offices. The Government of Canada adds that US dollars can be exchanged at most major banks, and that some ATMs accept Canadian debit cards with a four-digit PIN (five-digit PINs are not accepted).

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says Guatemala has one of the highest violent crime rates in Latin America, that carjacking and armed robbery are common, and that there have been armed attacks or robberies on most tourist routes between Guatemala City, Antigua, Tikal, Petén and Lake Atitlán. It advises against public buses, recommends radio-dispatched taxis, Uber or hotel taxis for short trips in towns, and advises not travelling alone or at night.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Guatemala travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: The UK Foreign Office says Guatemala's rainy season normally runs from May to November, the same time as the Caribbean hurricane season, with frequent flooding and landslides. The Government of Canada gives the rainy season as mid-May to mid-November and notes that forest fires occur between November and June, mostly in Petén.

idp.text: Guatemala is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Geneva, 1949), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3)

Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Guatemala yet.

tips.text: According to the UK Foreign Office, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua (the CA-4) share one 90-day stay: the period starts when you enter any of them and does not restart when you cross borders between them. You can extend by up to 30 days by paying a fee before the 90 days expire.
The Instituto Guatemalteco de Migración can extend a tourist stay (USD 25). Apply before your authorised stay runs out, or you will have to pay a fine for irregular stay.

PROATUR, the tourist assistance service of INGUAT, gives 24-hour emergency assistance and route advice to tourists, with staff who speak English and Spanish: call 1500 from inside Guatemala or +502 2290 2810 (UK Foreign Office).

The UK Foreign Office warns that some volcanoes are at high altitude with freezing temperatures at night, that local tour organisers tend to underestimate the risks, that deaths have occurred and that there is no mountain rescue service. Check INSIVUMEH (the meteorological office) and CONRED for access and restrictions before you climb.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guatemala?
faq.answer: Most Western travelers do not: the US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and most of the Americas enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Other nationalities need a consular visa (Category B), and some require a security-vetted consulted visa (Category C). Check your category with a Guatemalan consulate.

faq.question: How does the CA-4 90-day rule work in Guatemala?
faq.answer: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua share one 90-day stay. According to the UK Foreign Office, the period starts when you enter any of the four and does not restart when you cross borders between them. To stay longer you can extend by up to 30 days by paying a fee before the 90 days expire.

faq.question: Can I do a border run to reset my 90 days?
faq.answer: Not by crossing within the CA-4: the UK Foreign Office says the 90-day period does not restart when you cross borders between Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua. The official route to a longer stay is an extension of up to 30 days, paid for before the 90 days expire.

faq.question: Is Guatemala safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says Guatemala has one of the highest violent crime rates in Latin America, and that there have been armed attacks or robberies on most tourist routes between Guatemala City, Antigua, Tikal, Petén and Lake Atitlán. It advises against public buses (repainted US school buses), recommends radio-dispatched or hotel taxis for short trips, and points victims of crime to PROATUR (1500).

faq.question: What money should I use in Guatemala?
faq.answer: The quetzal (GTQ). No official source describes card acceptance. The UK Foreign Office says US dollars are much easier to exchange than British pounds and that it is safer to change money in hotels, banks or exchange offices because ATMs can be tampered with.
